title: A scaffolded brief passes the check meant to refuse an unbriefed fleet
foundBy: user report (host), asking why the stubs exist at all: "we are just adding more docs to keep in sync"
details:
`init` writes a brief for every member, and a brief nobody filled in passes validation.

A campaign scaffolded and left entirely untouched validates clean. Running validate on it prints a valid profile line and a mission digest beside a count of role briefs, with every blank still blank. The check behind that line asks whether the file exists. Nothing asks whether anyone wrote it.

R30 forbids a briefing of exactly this shape. A briefing that could be silently substituted for a generic one must not exist, because a member handed boilerplate restates the boilerplate faithfully and the readback cannot see through it. The scaffolding manufactures such a briefing, so `init` turns "no brief, refused" into "generic brief, accepted".

The stubs cost more than that. Each one restates guidance the playbook owns, so each is a second copy that can disagree with the first, and one already has. The mission stub named two outcome values the product does not have, which is SAC-021.

A stub also carries authoring guidance into the member. A stub's comments are written for the operator and reach the member verbatim, because nothing strips them. The digest recorded for a seeded file equals the sha256 of the raw file on disk. An author who fills in the blanks and leaves the scaffolding ships authoring guidance into a member's standing context.

The line worth drawing is whether a file is delivered. `profile.yaml` is never seeded, so its scaffolding is pure value and its comments reach nobody. `mission.md` and `roles/<member>.md` are delivered, and for those an empty directory refuses the campaign while a scaffolded blank does not.
